# gandalf

**Teaches the code changes behind each commit — multi-level, scroll-narrated lessons generated by Claude Code.**

A raw `git diff` shows *what* changed line-by-line but loses the **behavioral "what"** and the **"why."** gandalf takes a diff (any two refs, or `HEAD` vs your working tree), drives **Claude Code itself** (headless) to analyze it across four lenses — **behavioral**, **module-dependency**, **contract**, and **data-flow** — plus complexity, engineering-patterns, and active-recall material, and renders it as a beautiful, interactive, scroll-narrated web app. After a lesson you *understand* the change at every altitude, not just the diff.

Every metric is computed deterministically in Node and fed to Claude as ground truth (Claude interprets, never invents); every judgment is anchored to quoted lines.

> The techniques behind each format — and the program-comprehension, multimedia-learning, and retention research backing them — are documented in **[docs/RESEARCH.md](./docs/RESEARCH.md)**.

---

## 1. Installation

### Prerequisites

| Requirement | Why |
|---|---|
| **Node.js ≥ 20** | runtime (ESM + `tsx`) |
| **git** | gandalf reads diffs and history from a git repo |
| **Claude Code CLI**, installed and **logged in** | gandalf drives `claude -p` in headless mode and **reuses your existing Claude Code login** — it does **not** use an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |

Optional tools sharpen the deterministic metrics if present on your `PATH` (gandalf degrades gracefully without them): [`scc`](https://github.com/boyter/scc) (size/COCOMO), [`lizard`](https://github.com/terryyin/lizard) (per-function cyclomatic complexity, incl. Swift), `swiftlint` (Swift), [`difftastic`](https://github.com/Wilfred/difftastic).

### Install

```bash
git clone <repo-url> gandalf
cd gandalf
npm install
npm run build:web        # build the viewer — required for `gandalf serve` and `gandalf build`
```

Confirm Claude Code is ready:

```bash
claude --version         # should print a version; if not, install + log in to Claude Code first
```

(Recommended) install `gandalf` as a global command — this builds the viewer **and** drops a launcher on your `PATH`:

```bash
./scripts/install.sh                       # installs `gandalf` to ~/.local/bin
GANDALF_BIN_DIR=/usr/local/bin ./scripts/install.sh   # …or elsewhere
```

The launcher resolves Node itself (handy with `mise`/`nvm`), so `gandalf` works from **any directory** — including the non-interactive shells used by automation. Throughout this README, `npm run gandalf -- <cmd>` and `gandalf <cmd>` are interchangeable.

## 2. Running gandalf

### Generate a lesson

```bash
# default: HEAD vs the uncommitted working tree, analyzing the current repo
npm run gandalf -- generate

# any two refs
npm run gandalf -- generate --from <baseRef> --to <targetRef>

# scope to a ticket (overlays the ticket's intent as the "why")
npm run gandalf -- generate --ticket P1-003
```

Generation drives several `claude -p` calls (per-file passes + a fan-out of focused synthesis passes), so it **takes a few minutes and consumes Claude usage**. The resulting lesson is saved to:

```
<repo>/.gandalf/lessons/<id>/lesson.json
```

**`generate` options**

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--from <ref>` | `HEAD` | base ref |
| `--to <ref>` | *(working tree)* | target ref — omit to diff uncommitted changes |
| `--ticket <id>` | — | force a ticket id for the intent overlay |
| `--cwd <dir>` | current dir | repository to analyze |
| `--out-dir <dir>` | `<repo>/.gandalf/lessons` | where to write the lesson |
| `--model-file <m>` | `sonnet` | model for per-file passes |
| `--model-synth <m>` | `opus` | model for the synthesis passes |
| `--concurrency <n>` | `4` | parallel per-file passes |

### Browse lessons in the viewer

```bash
npm run gandalf -- serve            # http://localhost:4173
npm run gandalf -- serve --port 4300
```

Open the printed URL. The viewer lists every persisted lesson (newest first) in the **Lessons** menu.

### List persisted lessons

```bash
npm run gandalf -- list
```

### Check lesson integrity

```bash
npm run gandalf -- doctor              # all lessons
npm run gandalf -- doctor --lesson <id>
```

Reports cross-section drift (graph nodes that resolve to no file, contract/evidence references to unknown files, beacons past EOF, malformed diagrams). `generate` runs the same check automatically and prints warnings. Exit code 1 when errors are found.

### Export a self-contained lesson

```bash
npm run gandalf -- build --out lesson.html          # newest lesson
npm run gandalf -- build --lesson <id> --out lesson.html
```

See [§4](#4-exporting-a-static-asset).

---

## 3. Using / reading the lessons

Open a lesson in `gandalf serve`. Each lesson is a set of **lenses** (tabs), presented top-down — overview → zoom & filter → details on demand.

| Lens | What it answers |
|---|---|
| **Overview** | Verdict (behavioral vs refactor-only), breaking count, changed files, top hotspots |
| **Dependencies** | A module-dependency graph (color-coded by change). **Click a module** → its before/after TL;DR, contract deltas, and the diff |
| **Walkthrough** | A scroll-narrated tour: stepping prose on the left, a pinned code panel on the right with diff colouring (added = green, modified = yellow, removed = red marker) |
| **Behavioral** | The behavioral verdict, a one-line conditional-equivalence statement, and illustrative **Trace Cards** (input → before/after) |
| **Contracts** | Changed signatures with a Design-by-Contract **Safe / Breaking** verdict and pre/postcondition deltas |
| **Data flow** | A Mermaid sequence diagram + a Sankey of quantitative flow + before/after narrative |
| **Complexity** | Δ-scorecard, per-function before→after slope charts, and a hotspot treemap (area = churn, intensity = complexity) |
| **Patterns** | Design/architecture patterns & smells as a before→after delta, plus an ADR with "Considered Options" |
| **Recall** | Retrieval-practice questions to test (and retain) the change |

### Controls

- **Explain for** (ELI5 / Junior / Senior / Architect) — re-explains a lens at the chosen altitude. Shown only on lenses that have tiered text.
- **Quiz** (default on) — predict-then-reveal: guess the after-output / Safe-or-Breaking before it's shown. Toggle off to read passively.
- **Review** — spaced repetition over recall questions you've rated, across your whole lesson library.
- **+N / All files** — config/lockfile/dotfile noise is hidden by default; reveal it with this header toggle. Hidden files are also excluded from the complexity & hotspot metrics.
- **Maximize / Split** (Dependencies) — make the diff full-width, or switch to a GitHub-style before|after split.
- **Maximize** (Mermaid diagrams) — open a pan/zoom overlay (scroll to zoom, drag to pan).
- **Collapse hero** (chevron) — hide the title block to give the lenses more vertical room.
- **Dark mode** and the **Lessons** timeline live in the header (theme + depth tier persist).
- **Addressable views** — the URL tracks where you are (`#/lesson/<id>/<tab>`, plus the selected module on Dependencies, `#/library`, `#/tokens`), so reloads keep your place and links can be pasted/shared. Hash-based, so it also works in the offline single-file export.
- **Library** (header toggle) — a gallery landing page of every lesson as a cover card; click to open.
- **Share card** (in the lesson hero) — downloads a 1200×630 branded PNG of the lesson for posting.
- **Esc** resets any non-default view state (closes the diagram zoom, un-maximizes the diff).

> **Honesty note:** Trace Cards are reasoned from the code, **not executed** — they're labelled "illustrative." Every pattern/behavior claim carries quoted-line evidence and a confidence level.

## 4. Exporting a static asset

`gandalf build` inlines the viewer + a lesson into **one self-contained HTML file** that renders fully offline — no server, no network (fonts gracefully fall back to system fonts offline):

```bash
npm run gandalf -- build --lesson <id> --out lesson.html
```

### Attaching it to a GitHub PR / MR

GitHub (and GitLab) **don't render arbitrary HTML inline** in a review, and GitHub comment attachments reject raw `.html`. Practical options:

1. **Zip & attach** — `zip lesson.zip lesson.html`, then drag the `.zip` into a PR/MR comment. Reviewers download, unzip, and open `lesson.html` in any browser (works offline).
2. **CI artifact** — in CI, run `gandalf build` and upload `lesson.html` with `actions/upload-artifact`; reviewers download it from the run summary.
3. **Static host / Pages** — publish the file (GitHub Pages, S3, Netlify, …) and link it from the PR description.

Notes:
- The export embeds a **single** lesson; the spaced-**Review** feature in an export only sees that lesson.
- The file is large (everything is inlined). Prefer zipping for attachments.

## 5. Contributing

### Layout

```
bin/gandalf.ts        # commander CLI: generate | serve | build | list | doctor
src/core/             # engine: git · evidence · noise · tickets · claude · schemas · prompts · pipeline · lesson
src/server/serve.ts   # Hono server: static viewer + lesson API
web/                  # the React + Vite viewer (lenses, components, design tokens)
test/                 # engine unit tests (vitest)
scripts/              # Playwright visual-sanity harnesses
```

### Dev loop

```bash
npm run dev                       # Vite dev viewer (uses a bundled sample lesson; no server needed)
npm run typecheck                 # engine (tsc)
npm run typecheck:web             # viewer (tsc)
npm test                          # engine + lib unit tests (modules / noise / tickets / validate / claude shim / diff parser)
npm run build:web                 # production build of the viewer
```

The `scripts/*.mjs` Playwright harnesses screenshot the running viewer for visual review (they expect a `gandalf serve` instance and use the system Chrome).

### Conventions & constraints

- **TypeScript ESM** throughout; match the surrounding code's style.
- **Drive Claude only via the Claude Code CLI** (`claude -p`). Do **not** add the Agent SDK or the raw Messages API — both require an API key, which breaks the "reuse your Claude Code login" contract.
- **Two-plane analysis:** compute hard numbers deterministically in `src/core/evidence.ts`; Claude interprets them but never invents metrics. Keep judgments evidence-anchored.
- **Design system:** the viewer uses warm-editorial CSS-variable tokens — stay on the type/spacing/color/motion scales, keep **AA contrast in both themes**, honor **`prefers-reduced-motion`**, and keep new surfaces **dark-mode safe** (theme via CSS vars; re-render Shiki/Mermaid on theme change via `useIsDark`).
- Before opening a PR: `typecheck` + `typecheck:web` + the engine tests + `build:web` should pass, and a quick visual pass via the sanity scripts is appreciated.
